data.headline: Treasury curve flattens as the two-year yield rises
data.summary: From November 6 to 9, the two-year Treasury yield rose 5 basis points to 4.56% and the ten-year yield rose 2 to 4.88%. Their spread narrowed to 32 basis points. November 9 SOFR was 3.88%.

bull.text: November 9 SOFR was 1 basis point lower than November 6. Borrowers whose rates reset against SOFR can see some relief when credit spreads and contract terms are unchanged.

bear.text: The two-year yield rose from 4.51% to 4.56% and the ten-year rose from 4.86% to 4.88%. The ten-year minus two-year spread narrowed from 35 to 32 basis points.

watch.text: From October 27 to November 3, the net short held by leveraged funds in E-mini S&P 500 futures narrowed by 28,286 contracts to 372,318. Their net short in E-mini Russell 2000 futures widened by 6,999 contracts to 55,080.

limitations: The funding and Treasury series in this brief are dated November 9. The brief contains no verified ETF closing prices or returns.
The CFTC observations are weekly futures positions as of November 3. ETF flows and investor intent require separate evidence.
